steps: Pinch the tip of your dominant thumb and index finger together, leaving the other fingers extended.
Bring the pinched fingertips to the corner of your mouth, just beside your lips.
Push the hand forward away from your mouth in one smooth stroke, keeping the pinch closed.
Hold your palm angled roughly toward the person you are asking.
Mouth the word 'ask' as you push forward, with your eyebrows slightly raised.
tip: Think of catching the question at your lips and tossing it to the listener.

steps: Make an open pinched handshape with your dominant hand, thumb and fingertips held apart.
Start the hand a short distance in front of your chest, palm roughly facing sideways.
Pull the hand back toward your chest in one decisive motion while closing the pinch shut.
Keep the movement single and firm, like plucking one option out of the air.
Pair it with a decided expression and mouth 'choose' as your hand closes.
tip: One pull, one close — the sign grabs the option and brings it home to you.

steps: Extend the index and middle fingers of your dominant hand, folding the other fingers away.
Hold the two extended fingers in front of your body, palm facing sideways like scissors blades.
Open and close the two fingers repeatedly in a small, quick snipping motion.
Drift the hand slightly forward as you snip, tracing the line of the cut.
Pair the sign with a neutral expression and mouth 'cut' while you snip.
tip: The same sign also covers scissors — BSL CUT mimes the tool doing the job.

steps: Hold both hands open and flat in front of your chest, palms facing toward you.
Cross your hands at the wrists while keeping the palms facing inward.
Sweep both hands upward and outward in a wide arc, as if tracing the rising sun.
Finish with your hands apart at about shoulder height, palms still facing you.
Keep a neutral expression and mouth 'day' as the arc completes.
tip: The sunrise arc is the memory hook — crossed hands uncross like dawn breaking.

steps: Hold your non-dominant hand open and flat in front of your chest, palm facing upward.
Point your dominant index finger down into the hollow where the base hand's thumb meets the palm.
Hold the position steady for a beat — YEAR is fingerspelled as the letter Y, not signed.
Mouth the word 'year' clearly while you hold the letter shape.
tip: A single-letter fingerspell standing in for a whole word is normal for BSL time units.
